chunks.text: PatchRot works as follows. Take an input image and either rotate the whole image, or rotate each of its patches independently, by a random multiple of ninety degrees: zero, ninety, one-eighty, or two-seventy.

chunks.text: The vision transformer is then trained to predict these rotation angles as a simple four-way classification. The transformer's class token, which normally predicts the object category, is repurposed to predict the whole-image rotation, capturing global structure.

chunks.text: New multilayer-perceptron heads are attached to each patch token to predict that individual patch's rotation, capturing local detail. To prevent the network from cheating, patches are carved from a slightly larger grid and randomly cropped, so a random buffer gap sits between them and edge continuity can't give away the answer.
